lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Job Readiness: Applications, Resumes, and Interviews
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: practising common interview questions

objective: Learners practice answering five common entry-level interview questions out loud with a trusted adult playing the interviewer, then revise their weakest answer, so they can speak about their own experience clearly under mild real-time pressure.
scenario: A trusted adult plays interviewer using five provided common questions (such as 'tell me about yourself' and 'why do you want this job'), the learner answers out loud without reading from a script, and the adult gives brief specific feedback on one answer to revise.
safetyNotes: No audio or video recording of the practice interview is made; the adult gives feedback live and the learner writes notes afterward.
The adult's role is supportive practice, not a real evaluation of the learner as a person; keep feedback about the answers, not about the learner's confidence or character.

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available to play interviewer at this time, the learner instead writes out full answers to all five questions, then reads them aloud once to themselves and checks each answer against the same look-fors a live interviewer would use, marking which ones they think are strong and which need work.

materials: the five provided common interview questions
paper or notes app for revising the weakest answer

tasks.directions: Before practicing out loud, jot a one-line note on what you'd say for each of the five questions.

prompts.text: For each of the five questions, write one sentence of what you'd say. You don't need full answers yet.

tasks.directions: With your adult playing interviewer, answer all five questions out loud without reading a script.

prompts.text: I answered all five questions out loud without reading directly from notes.
My adult gave specific feedback on one answer to revise.

tasks.directions: Revise your weakest answer based on the feedback and write the improved version.

prompts.text: Write your revised answer to the question you're revising, and explain in one sentence what specifically you changed.
Which of the five questions felt hardest to answer out loud, and why do you think that one was harder than the others?

remediation: If the learner's answers are too short to give an interviewer anything to work with (a few words, no example), reteach using the pattern 'state it, back it with one specific example, connect it to the job,' modeling the pattern on the easiest question first, then have the learner retry two questions using that pattern before moving on.
extension: Have the learner add two harder, less common questions (such as 'describe a time you made a mistake at something' or 'how do you handle being told no') to the practice round and answer those as well, using the same feedback-and-revise process.
